title: Hippolytus of Rome, Chronicon (Συναγωγὴ χρόνων καὶ ἐτῶν, including the Diamerismos; «Хроника» Ипполита Римского)
author: Hippolytus of Rome
language: Greek (Matritensis gr. 121), plus Latin versions (Liber generationis I–II)
genre: Christian world chronicle with an ethnographic-geographic catalogue of peoples, lands and islands
size: Greek text est. 15–20k words, not counting the Stadiasmus. GCS 46 c. 200 pp. including the Latin versions
edition: A. Bauer, TU 29.1 (1905): public domain. Bauer–Helm, GCS 46 (2nd ed. 1955): in copyright
ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Ипполит Римский) lists about 20 Russian translations (Refutatio, Antichrist, Apostolic Tradition, etc.); none is of the Chronicon. No Russian found
en_evidence: Only an online 'rough draft' English translation by T. C. Schmidt & N. Nicholas (2010), per en.wikipedia. No published English found
value: The earliest surviving Christian world chronicle. Its Diamerismos (the division of the earth among Noah's sons) is a foundational text of late-antique ethnography and geography, used by the Paschale, Synkellos and Georgios Monachos. Matters to classicists, historians of geography and scholars of early Christianity.
ai_feasibility: High: plain Greek and lists. Needs gazetteer linking (Pleiades/ToposText) and collation with the Latin versions
pilot_unit: The Diamerismos with its catalogues of peoples, languages and islands, est. 4–6k words
